study_identification_part.si_4_title: Delineating the Heterogeneity of Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Normative Models of Dynamic Brain Functional Networks

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study uses three datasets: (1) Cam-CAN (Cambridge Centre for Aging and Neuroscience) as Dataset 1 with 644 healthy individuals for building the normative model; (2) MCAD (Multicenter Alzheimer Disease Imaging Consortium) as Dataset 2 with 257 NC, 257 MCI, and 295 AD patients from 7 sites; (3) ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) as Dataset 3 with 259 NC and 184 MCI patients for longitudinal validation.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) scans of 1896 individuals were acquired from 3 datasets. Dataset 1, which included 644 healthy individuals, was used in this work to build a normative model and was obtained from the Cambridge Centre for Aging and Neuroscience repository (Cam-CAN)... Dataset 2 comprised 257 normal control (NC) participants, 257 patients with MCI, and 295 patients with AD from the MCAD (Multicenter Alzheimer Disease Imaging Consortium) dataset. Dataset 3 included 259 NC participants and 184 patients with MCI from the ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) database..."
